metadata.title: Lynx - AI Agent Debugging and Reliability
metadata.description: Lynx helps teams trace AI agent conversations, LLM calls, tool calls, and errors in a session timeline to analyze and reproduce production issues.

header.homeAria: Go to the Lynx introduction page

hero.headline: Trace and debug production issues in AI support and agent workflows.
hero.description: Lynx connects conversations, LLM calls, tool calls, errors, latency, and cost into one session flow. When something goes wrong, teams can inspect root cause candidates quickly and keep evidence that can be reproduced.
hero.trustNote: We are currently discussing product direction, feedback, and pilots with teams operating AI agents.

timeline.label: Session timeline
timeline.value: Trace conversations, LLM calls, and tool/API calls in one flow.

rootCause.label: Issue analysis
rootCause.value: See which input, response, knowledge step, or task introduced the issue.

debugging.label: Reproducible debugging
debugging.value: Check whether an issue can repeat and connect it to operational improvements.

problem.title: As AI enters real services and workflows, operational issues become more complex.
problem.body1: AI features now go beyond simple response generation and operate together with internal knowledge, business rules, and external tools. When wrong answers, bad calls, exceptions, or policy violations happen, raw logs are rarely enough to understand the cause quickly.
problem.body2: When AI affects real user experiences or business workflows, teams need a structure for analyzing the cause and reproducing the issue after it happens.

features.title: Find where an error happened quickly, then reproduce it with evidence.

timeline.title: Session timeline
timeline.body: Connect conversations, LLM calls, tool calls, and errors into one flow so teams can see where an issue started.

rootCause.title: Root cause candidates
rootCause.body: Surface the input, response, retrieval step, or tool call that likely introduced the issue, with evidence attached.

improve.title: Reproduce and improve
improve.body: Check whether an issue is one-off or repeatable, then connect the finding to guardrail and prompt improvements.

reliability.title: Operational safety
reliability.body: Use async SDK delivery, circuit breakers, and local buffering so Lynx server problems do not take down customer services.

audience.title: Built for teams like these
audience.body: Lynx is for teams building products where AI features are deeply connected to real services and operational flows. It is especially useful when teams need to trace issues quickly and improve them in a repeatable way.

examples.support: Teams operating AI features that interact directly with users
examples.toolAgents: Teams running AI workflows connected to external tools or internal systems
examples.b2b: AI product teams where quality, reliability, and operational visibility matter

flow.title: Lynx looks at one execution flow, not isolated logs.

record.title: Record
record.body: Connect the user request, LLM calls, tool actions, and policy decisions in one session.

inspect.title: Inspect
inspect.body: Show the context before failure with root cause candidates so teams can narrow the issue.

control.title: Control
control.body: Manage risky tool actions and repeated calls with runtime policies.

preview.title: Track the session where the issue happened.
preview.body: Lynx organizes an AI agent's execution into a session timeline so operators and developers can find the point of failure quickly.

finalCta.title: We are looking for teams to validate AI operational quality with us.
finalCta.body: Lynx is currently an early MVP, and we are discussing product direction, feedback, and pilots with teams that connect AI features to real services and operational workflows.
finalCta.note: We would like to talk with teams interested in incident analysis, reproducible debugging, and operational reliability.
